text:
kyle (product): Brain-dump: long-term work for routing + multi-region + tenant isolation. We need a productized "lane" concept (latency, balanced, economical, burst) + per-route capacity reservations and a compliance-ready isolation bundle. Aiming for pilot in ~3 months. Initial scope ideas?

anya (eng-platform): +1. Important to separate two things: policy (declarative decisions) and execution (routing+placement). Policies drive selectors and allowed fallbacks; execution needs pre-reservation and eviction semantics.

rach (arch): Propose a minimal manifest v0: selector, allowed_regions, lane, reserved_qps(optional), fallback_policy, lock, audit_level. Make precedence deterministic. Example: 
```
route "org:beta/chat" {
  allowed_regions: ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"]
  lane: "latency"
  reserved_qps: 50
  fallback: {region:"us-east-1",model:"small-q4"}
  lock: true
  audit_level: "signed"
}
```
Audit must include (decision, reason, cache_hit, signed_by).

samir (infra): Operational notes: reserved_qps implies capacity reservations in dedicated pools or token buckets across regions. Cross-region fallback = cold KV-cache + egress. We should define prefetch heuristics and an opt-in pre-warm plan for reserved prefixes. Also track egress billing per-customer when crossing regions.

tess (solutions): From customers: 1) enterprise customers want signed attestations that routing never crossed jurisdiction X; 2) some want per-route capacity guarantees for launch week; 3) others want a cheap "burst" lane that uses lower-priority capacity and accepts higher p99. We should map each to acceptance criteria.

noah (sales): I have two pilots willing to try per-route reservations + pinning if we can show: measured p95/p99, failover delta, and an isolation artifact for audits. They'll want a 6-week trial window.

anya (eng-platform): Risk: fallback storms when a region loses capacity. Need global backoff + graceful degradation: e.g., degrade model size, increase quantization, or queue with a best-effort SLA. Also need a per-tenant throttle and emergency routing-freeze.

rach (arch): Suggest we version the manifest and provide a compatibility checker. Also define conflict resolution: most-specific selector wins; if equal specificity, highest reserved_qps wins; locked routes cannot be overridden without explicit ops confirmation.

samir (infra): I'll prototype: (a) reserved_qps enforcement design; (b) pre-warm estimator for KV cache given prefix QPS; (c) egress cost model for cross-region fallbacks. ETA 10 business days.

tess (solutions): I'll assemble three customer requirement docs and produce mapping to launch gates (1 week). Include compliance checklist: routing logs, KMS binding evidence, signed attestations, and migration runbook.

noah (sales): I'll recruit pilots and negotiate instrumentation access. Target two pilots by EOM.

racha (arch): Example of graceful fallback policy concept: fallback can be prioritized: [{region:us-east-1,model:small-q4},{region:eu-west-1,model:quant-small,prewarm:true}]. If prewarm:true we trigger async prefix fetch.

anya (eng-platform): Implementation notes: policy engine should support dry-run, atomic apply, and a canary window (e.g., 5m) before full rollout. Also expose decision metrics: route_chosen, lat_ms, cache_hit, fallback_reason.

samir (infra): We'll need a tooling hook to precompute warmup time given prefix popularity and a slider for prewarm aggressiveness vs egress cost. Will include a heatmap sim (spiky/steady/seasonal).

kyle (product): Draft pilot gates (v0):
- two pilots using per-route reservations or pinned regions
- lane definitions + measured SLOs per lane (p95/p99)
- reserved_qps enforcement + observed behavior under spike
- migration runbook + rollback (shared -> reserved/dedicated)
- policy manifest v0 + UI for basic edits and dry-run
- routing audit export + signed attestations bundle for private deployments

anya (eng-platform): Add gate: emergency routing-freeze API and per-tenant fallback opt-out.

rach (arch): We'll provide manifest schema + compatibility docs and a precedence matrix.

samir (infra): Deliverables: reserved_qps design doc, prewarm estimator + sim results, egress cost sketch. ETA 10d.

tess (solutions): Deliverables: 3 customer docs mapped to gates; compliance artifact checklist (1w).

noah (sales): Deliverable: two pilot commitments + scoped SLA for pilot instrumentation (ASAP).

deploy-bot: scheduled: infra/experiment/reservations-proto deploy started by rach at 2025-02-14T09:00:00Z

kyle (product): I'll assemble milestones + gating table and post in #product-docs by Friday. Anything else we should call out now?

anya (eng-platform): One more: telemetry contract must be explicit (fields, sampling, retention) so pilots and audits are consistent.

rach (arch): Also: define eviction semantics clearly (LRU vs priority-based) and document customer-visible behavior on eviction during saturation.

kyle (product): Great. Thanks all 44D. I'll create the project brief and link this thread. If you have must-haves, drop them here or DM.
